title: German researchers call for computer science to reinvent itself as "Computer and AI Science"
title_en: German researchers call for computer science to reinvent itself as "Computer and AI Science"
author: Alan Truly
content_snippet:
AI can significantly accelerate software development and automate parts of the process. That makes traditional computer science more important, not less, 40 researchers at the Technical University of Darmstadt argue. They want the field to evolve into "Computer and AI Science,"because AI is becoming a core technology for building and using tomorrow's computer systems.

The researchers are affiliated with the university's Department of Computer Science and lay out their case in a joint position p
summary_en: Researchers at the Department of Computer Science at the Technical University of Darmstadt published a position paper advocating for the transition of the field into 'Computer and AI Science.' The proposal highlights that generative computing shifts software development from manual coding to the oversight and validation of AI-generated systems, necessitating a fundamental rethink of software verification and runtime certification.

title_en: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents review, fix, and approve pull requests on their own
author: Maximilian Schreiner
content_snippet:

The system pairs the already available Code Review feature for catching bugs with two new AI agents called PR Steward and Claude Approvals.

summary_en: Anthropic launched the beta of Claude Ship, a toolset including Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals to automate the analysis, remediation, and merging of code changes. The system executes compliance decisions based on local policy files, enabling fully autonomous, human-free code deployments for routine updates.

title: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns
title_en: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns

inline_images.caption: Mr. Trump has become personally acquainted with Mr. Huang and considers him an ally. (Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Mr. Trump has become personally acquainted with Mr. Huang and considers him an ally.

author: Peter Baker
content_snippet:
By his own account, President Trump was watching the stock market slide and decided to stop it. He would take it upon himself to determine who should lead one of the nation’s largest companies. Never mind national security concerns, never mind the autonomy of the private sector. Mr. Trump would decide.

The president’s extraordinary intervention resulted in Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as chief executive of Nvidia on Monday, just 11 days after he was forced out amid a Chinese espionage scandal.
summary_en: President Trump forced the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia after his 11-day ouster following allegations of ties to a Chinese intelligence asset. Despite warnings from intelligence agencies, Trump cited stock market stabilization as his primary motivation, sparking intense scrutiny in Washington over the intersection of critical tech leadership and national security.

content_snippet:
On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watchtower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. None of these things are visible on Google Maps. Where drivers see a checkpoint, a barrier, and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear.

author: Wall Street Journal
content_snippet:
French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. The attack affected about 700 supermarkets, raising concerns about the exposure of connected refrigeration systems and the potential for cyber operations to disrupt essential commercial infrastructure.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot
summary_en: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot officially attributed the cyberattack on over 700 European supermarket refrigeration controllers to Iran's 'SHAHID KAVEH' cyber unit during a G7 meeting. The attack, occurring between October 11-12, caused widespread equipment failures, fires, and tens of millions of euros in food losses, marking a transition from espionage to physical infrastructure sabotage.

author: Reuters
content_snippet:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US lawmakers from both parties offered sharp criticism on Monday of Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and said Congress must pass legislation to crack down on US chip exports to China and get answers.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Banking Committee starting in January, called the decision to reinstate Huang "reckless," adding the board still owes Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls

title: Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
title_en: Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
author: James Temple
content_snippet:
Tech companies are investing a lot of hope and money in rocks.

Google, Microsoft, and others have committed hundreds of millions of dollars to get startups to spread crushed basalt, olivine, or other alkaline materials across farms, in an effort to capture carbon from the air and lock it away. A number of influential models have found that this approach, known as enhanced rock weathering (ERW), could eventually remove 3 billion to 8 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide per year, helping to slo
summary_en: Research by CarbonPlan suggests that 'Enhanced Rock Weathering' (ERW), a climate solution heavily backed by Google and Microsoft, faces significant scalability challenges. The study indicates that spreading basalt or olivine at levels required for climate impact may degrade soil health and decrease crop yields; scaling back applications to protect harvests would likely cap the method's CO2 removal potential to under 1 billion tons per year.
title_zh: 岩石风化固碳技术存在减产隐患
summary_zh: 碳捕获技术方案“增强岩石风化”研究显示，大规模铺设矿石可能导致农作物产量下降，削减其碳封存潜能

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 由CarbonPlan发布的研究显示，被谷歌与微软寄予厚望的“增强岩石风化”（ERW）技术存在商业化隐患。研究发现，在农田大量铺设玄武岩或橄榄石以捕捉二氧化碳，在达到有效碳封存规模的同时，可能对土壤质量产生负面影响，进而导致农作物减产。若为保证粮食产量而减少矿石施用量，该方案的固碳年容量预计将降至10亿吨以下。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Research by CarbonPlan suggests that 'Enhanced Rock Weathering' (ERW), a climate solution heavily backed by Google and Microsoft, faces significant scalability challenges. The study indicates that spreading basalt or olivine at levels required for climate impact may degrade soil health and decrease crop yields; scaling back applications to protect harvests would likely cap the method's CO2 removal potential to under 1 billion tons per year.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】CarbonPlan（碳研究机构）、Google、Microsoft在农业土地治理与碳移除项目：指出增强岩石风化法可能导致农作物减产，限制了其碳移除规模
【起因与机理】技术在追求气候效益的同时，忽视了对土壤生态系统长期产出的干扰
【关键数据与实测】若为保证粮食产量而减少矿石施用量，该方案的固碳年容量预计将降至10亿吨以下。
【各方立场与态度】此项研究对碳移除市场的估值逻辑提出了严厉审视，未来大规模固碳项目需强制纳入环境负面溢出效应的量化审计，避免陷入“气候补救破坏食品安全”的商业死循环。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] CarbonPlan, Google, Microsoft: Identified potential crop yield reductions from large-scale rock weathering, limiting carbon sequestration scalability
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Climate benefits potentially conflict with long-term soil health and agricultural productivity
[Key Metrics] One recent study found that ERW boosted the median yields of smallholder farmers in India by more than 20%.

[Industry Impact & Outlook] This research challenges current valuation models in carbon markets, necessitating that large-scale sequestration projects include mandatory environmental impact audits to prevent a conflict between climate mitigation and food security.

author: Chris Buckley
content_snippet:
When Xi Jinping, the Chinese leader, set about expanding China’s nuclear forces a decade ago, his goal was to ensure that enough missiles could survive an initial attack so Beijing could deliver a devastating counterattack.

That ability to withstand a strike and hit back would deter any enemy from risking nuclear blackmail or war against China in the first place, Chinese strategists have said.

But now, researchers in the Chinese military worry that American advances in artificial intelligence
summary_en: Researchers at the Academy of Military Science in Beijing warn that the U.S. integration of AI into nuclear decision-making could compress response times from 15-30 minutes to under 90 seconds. This capability sparks concerns that U.S. forces may achieve superior precision in detecting and neutralizing Chinese nuclear assets, thereby undermining Beijing's second-strike deterrence.
